experiment: SenCache native LTX 0.9.6 sensitivity recalibration using eight real Mixkit videos

generation.negative_prompt: worst quality, inconsistent motion, blurry, jittery, distorted

calibration_cases.prompt: Water in slow motion flows down the river creating a foam and waves through the rocks
Crowds of people cross a street junction
A dog resting on the grass next to a dog toy
Top view of a woman slicing vegetables
One on one in a soccer game

fresh_evaluation_cases.prompt: Pacific coast, carmel by the sea ocean and waves.
An astronaut flying in space, zoom out
a sink on the right of a toilet, front view
a carrot on the top of a hot dog, front view

historical_evaluation_cases.prompt: A fluffy orange cat walks across a sunlit room and gently brushes its tail against the leg of a wooden chair. A steady low camera follows the natural walking motion, with realistic fur and consistent warm light.

A woman in a blue jacket jogs at a relaxed pace along a riverside path. Her arms move naturally as the camera tracks smoothly from the side, with coherent proportions and detailed trees in soft daylight.

A close view of two hands slowly pouring clear water from a small glass pitcher into a ceramic cup on a wooden kitchen counter. The water stream and fingers remain visible throughout a continuous steady realistic shot.

A red tram moves slowly along rails past a row of old brick buildings. The camera stays steady at street level, showing smooth wheel motion and changing reflections in the windows under soft afternoon light.

source.selection: First freely licensed landscape clip in each of eight prespecified Mixkit categories, in the archived 2026-11-07 category pages; eligibility checked before sensitivity or evaluation results.
source.caption_source: Mixkit item title; no model-generated caption or outcome-based editing.
source.paper_size_ablation: 8 versus 4096 diverse videos; close sensitivity profiles reported

estimator.J_x: ||f(x_next,t)-f(x,t)||2 / ||x_next-x||2; x_next is one native deterministic scheduler step using positive-conditional f(x,t)
estimator.input: Eight real Mixkit RGB videos, uniformly sampled and resized as in upstream; native LTX 0.9.6 VAE posterior with per-channel normalization.
estimator.model_output: Full conditional Transformer output after output projection, matching upstream estimator (not hidden residual norm)
estimator.timesteps: All 50 actual native scheduled noise levels, continuous model inputs; table uses 1000*sigma to match existing lookup
estimator.precision: BF16 model inputs/weights; native inference arithmetic; FP32 differences and norms; FP64 CPU aggregation
estimator.aggregation: Arithmetic mean per timestep across eight clips; snapshots after1,4,8; report per-clip variation without treating a4/8 comparison as proof of convergence.
estimator.guidance: Positive conditional Transformer output, as upstream; text condition is the unmodified Mixkit item title.

limitations: Source and number match the SenCache paper (eight Mixkit videos); the authors exact clip identities were not found in the public paper, repository or released sensitivity files. These are our prespecified eight clips.
Shape, frame count, fps and native noise schedule match our evaluated LTX 0.9.6 setup, not the papers LTX 0.9.1 experiment settings.
The published result supporting eight samples is motivation, not a guarantee of convergence on this checkpoint and shape.
The12 paired test cases are a limited validation, not a replacement for the complete benchmark in the paper.
Old/new tables differ in clip identities, shape, schedule and checkpoint version; this is not a version-only causal ablation.
No threshold selection or clip selection uses evaluation outcomes; a lower or higher quality outcome is retained.

switch.reason: User selected eight Mixkit videos to follow official paper source and sample count with low preparation cost.

preprocessing.note: Upstream temporal selection and spatial resize, with target shape/fps fixed to our evaluated LTX 0.9.6 setting.

randomness.assignment: Round-robin over eight fixed clips; one run per clip, not three replicas.
randomness.noise: One generator per clip, seeded with its assigned training seed; draw successively across 50 steps.
randomness.generation: No synthetic calibration video generation; seeds only affect VAE posterior and perturbation noise.
